book.palaneogenesis.category.items.descr: Every item added by the mod, what it does, and how to craft it.
Long before the powers known today existed, villages lived under the protection of ancient guardians. Káak Tun was one of them.$(br2)For years he protected primitive villages as the world slowly fell into chaos, watching wars, invasions, and creatures that drove the old peoples from their homes.

The Nether became a threat. The End became a threat. And the villages he had sworn to protect disappeared, one by one.$(br2)Káak Tun remained. Time turned the warrior into an elder, but it could never take his strength or his wisdom from him.

Now he has returned. He dwells among the villages once more, still keeping the oath he made centuries ago: to protect them.$(br2)But Káak Tun understands something the old warriors never could - the power of the past is no longer alone. Something from the future has begun to meet it, and Steve stands right in the middle of that convergence.
A tireless guardian. Wherever a village stands, a Káak Tun is never far - watching over it exactly as he always has.

Despite his imposing size, Káak Tun never attacks the player - not even in retaliation if struck first. His only enemies are the hostile creatures that threaten the village he guards.$(br2)With 300 health and armor to match a full set of diamond, he is far tougher than an Iron Golem, and just as unshakeable in his purpose.

Once a hostile mob draws near, Káak Tun answers with two attacks: a heavy melee strike at close range, and a charged beam fired at anything within reach after a couple of seconds spent taking aim.$(br2)The melee blow is deliberately the stronger of the two - Káak Tun always prefers to finish a fight up close.

A Blue Heart can be earned from Káak Tun in two ways. The peaceful route: feed him Lapis Lazuli - four offerings are rewarded with a single heart, freely given.$(br2)The other way is combat: since Káak Tun never strikes first, any battle is a choice the player makes - and defeating him always leaves a Blue Heart behind.
book.palaneogenesis.entry.items.blue_hea: The Blue Heart represents the ancient guardians: simple, resilient warriors determined to remain standing.$(br2)They needed no extraordinary powers. Their greatest virtue was endurance - taking one blow, then another, and continuing to advance.

The Blue Heart carries that legacy: the strength of those who didn't need to defeat the enemy quickly. They only needed to survive it.$(br2)While transformed, using a Blue Heart grants a small amount of temporary life - and nothing else. No duration, no side effects: it's the most basic safeguard the ancient power offers.

Blue Hearts are earned from $(l:mobs/kaak_tun)Káak Tun$() - offered peacefully in exchange for Lapis Lazuli, or left behind after a fight.$(br2)They have no crafting recipe of their own, but every other heart in this guide - and the Ancient Extract Syringe itself - requires at least one to create.
book.palaneogenesis.entry.items.empty_sy: The Empty Syringe serves two purposes. Combined with the right ingredients, it becomes the base for an Ancient Extract Syringe - but once the player is transformed, using an Empty Syringe on its own ends the transformation instead.$(br2)Reverting shatters the syringe: what remains afterward is a $(l:items/broken_syringe)Broken Syringe$().
book.palaneogenesis.entry.items.ancient_: This is where the transformation begins. Injecting the Ancient Extract Syringe channels the power of the past directly into Steve's body.$(br2)The change is immediate: maximum health collapses to a single half-heart, but in its place Steve gains a reserve of temporary life - the same currency stored in every Blue Heart - along with a lasting boost to speed and attack strength for as long as the transformation holds.

Unlike most items in this guide, the Ancient Extract Syringe isn't made at a crafting table. An $(l:items/empty_syringe)Empty Syringe$() is dipped in a source of Water together with Lapis Lazuli, Blackstone, and a $(l:items/blue_heart)Blue Heart$() to complete the process.

Transforming and reverting back and forth too quickly comes at a cost: toggling five times within a few seconds permanently costs Steve one full heart of maximum health, though it can never fall below one whole heart.$(br2)To revert safely, use an $(l:items/empty_syringe)Empty Syringe$() while transformed.
book.palaneogenesis.entry.items.broken_s: What's left of an $(l:items/empty_syringe)Empty Syringe$() after it's used to end a transformation - a spent, shattered shell rather than a reusable container.$(br2)It can't be refilled or used for anything else. A fresh Empty Syringe has to be crafted before the ancient power can be channeled again.
book.palaneogenesis.entry.items.explosiv: Some warriors knew perfectly well that they could die - and fought anyway. For them, death didn't mean leaving the battle. It meant turning their final instant into a weapon.$(br2)Many would have called them kamikazes. Those waiting for them back home called them heroes.

The Explosive Heart carries that sacrifice. While transformed, using one grants a small amount of temporary life, same as any other heart - but when a point of it breaks in combat, it detonates around Steve, destroying nearby hostile mobs without damaging a single block.
book.palaneogenesis.entry.items.resistan: Other warriors understood that resisting didn't simply mean enduring. Every battle made them stronger; every blow prepared them for the next.$(br2)The warriors of the resistance advanced as their bodies and their will adapted to war itself.

A single Resistance Heart alone grants only a modest edge. But as more points build up at once, its passive effect grows with them - resistance gradually turning into raw mining speed - and breaking a point grants a burst of Resistance.
book.palaneogenesis.entry.items.inverted: And there were those who received something no warrior should ever have carried: a malevolent power, capable of consuming them from within.$(br2)They refused to let it decide their fate. Instead of being destroyed by it, they did the impossible - they inverted their own heart. What should have destroyed them became what would destroy their enemies instead.

The Inverted Heart has no active effect of its own. But when a point of it breaks, it drains the life from every hostile creature for a huge distance around Steve - sparing only the Ender Dragon - striking each one down with a burst of ash and soul rather than an explosion.
book.palaneogenesis.entry.items.kaak_tun: A standard spawn egg for $(l:mobs/kaak_tun)Káak Tun$(), available only in Creative mode.$(br2)It has no crafting recipe - it exists purely to place a guardian directly, rather than waiting for one to appear near a village.
book.palaneogenesis.entry.items.ancient_: This transformation takes full ownership of Steve's maximum health while it holds, overwriting whatever value was there before. This is deliberate: other artifacts or curses that also alter maximum health are not merged with this one - they simply give way to it for as long as the transformation lasts, and return to normal once it ends.
